scope: Existing official native baseline12 versus DI400; no new generation. Same retained shared first images/settings; not an isolated one-module training comparison.

captions.VP026: Two people stretch a bungee cord, extending it to its maximum length.
captions.VP031: A tightly folded parachute is unfolded, revealing its vibrant colors and intricate design.
captions.VP036: A slow-motion view of the jump showing leg extension and body position.
captions.VP051: A billiard ball is struck and rolls across a felt-covered pool table, hitting another ball.

observations.VP026: Native grows disembodied arms and rearranges cables; DI mostly keeps initial sea/cable apparatus static. Image/target object consistency needs consideration; suppressing hallucination alone is not successful process completion.
observations.VP036: Both remain close to initial airborne split pose across sampled frames; neither shows a completed flight/landing. Native itself is not a successful process reference.
observations.VP031: Native changes canopy colors and inflates into large colorful geometry; DI also changes colors/shape to a red/green circular object. Neither establishes retained identity plus correct deployment.
observations.VP051: Native changes scene/composition and adds/mutates billiard balls; DI retains composition but ball/process mostly static and later surface identity changes. Both contain quality/process failures.

conclusion: Native generation is not uniformly visually valid on these shared I2V inputs. DI trades some scene stability for weak process execution; preserving native channels alone cannot establish final quality. Review first-image/request consistency without silently replacing shared benchmark inputs or reporting mixed protocols.
